title: Most negatively geared investors have taxable incomes below $100,000
oneLiner: Tax office data is cited to show the concession is used mainly by middle earners, not the wealthy.
body: Tax statistics show that the majority of individuals reporting a net rental loss have taxable incomes under $100,000. Defenders of the concession cite this to argue it is a middle-class saving tool rather than a tax break for the rich.
contextBackground: This claim has been reverted repeatedly because 'income' is doing contested work. Taxable income is measured after the rental loss is deducted, so a high earner with a large loss appears as a middle earner. Measured by total income before deductions, the distribution tilts upward.
contextDisagreement: Both readings of the tax data are accurate; they measure different things. The dispute is over which measure the claim should use, and whether the claim as worded misleads.

contested.reason: Three reverts by different users inside 24 hours, over whether 'income' means taxable income after deductions or total income before them. Edits from non-moderators queue for review until the quiet period ends.

evidenceItems.citation: Australian Taxation Office, Taxation statistics — individuals by taxable income range, net rent

otherClaim.title: Parliament should pass the 2026 budget's restriction of negative gearing to newly built homes

claimItself.title: Parliament should pass the 2026 budget's restriction of negative gearing to newly built homes
claimItself.oneLiner: The policy is now a bill before the Senate: negative gearing for new builds only from July 2027, existing investors grandfathered, and a reworked capital gains discount alongside it.
claimItself.body: The 12 May 2026 budget restricted negative gearing to newly built residential property for investments made after budget night, with effect from 1 July 2027, and replaced the 50 per cent capital gains discount with an inflation-based discount and a 30 per cent floor. Anyone using the concessions before budget night keeps them. A Senate inquiry took evidence in June 2026.
